title: Burj Al Arab
blurb: Dubai’s sail-shaped luxury hotel in simplified schematic form: a 321 m sail on an artificial island, 202 duplex suites around a 180 m atrium, and a cantilevered helipad.

systems.name: Island and foundations
systems.description: The artificial island 280 m offshore: a simplified slab with its rock armor ring, the surrounding sea surface, and the causeway to the shore.

systems.name: Podium and entrance
systems.description: The lobby block and entry canopy at island level.

systems.name: Suites
systems.description: The 202 duplex suites as two simplified tower blocks with window bands, a backbone spine, the Royal penthouse and crown blocks.

systems.name: Sail and mast
systems.description: The Teflon-coated fabric sail as a single billowing curtain with ribs, and the steel V simplified to one tapered mast needle with braces and beacon.

systems.name: Atrium
systems.description: The 180 m atrium as a single void volume with simplified marble pillars.

systems.name: Restaurants and bars
systems.description: The sky pod restaurant on its cantilever arm, the aquarium tank restaurant, and the deck terrace standing in for the North Deck.

systems.name: Helipad
systems.description: The cantilevered helipad at 210 m: a disc on a simplified support arm.

systems.name: Services
systems.description: Lift shafts, merged plant boxes, bridge lights along the causeway, and the terrace pool.

explanations.island slab: The artificial island the hotel stands on, about 150 m per side and rising about 7.5 m above the waves, shown here as a simplified slab. Exact outline is schematic.
explanations.rock armor ring: The ring of rock bunds and protective armor around the island against wave erosion. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.sea surface: The Arabian Gulf around the island, about 280 m from Jumeirah Beach. Water level and extent are schematic.
explanations.causeway to shore: The private curving bridge to the mainland, the hotel’s only land link, with its piers merged into one part. Length and curve are schematic.
explanations.lobby block: The lobby block at the base of the atrium. Exact glazing is schematic.
explanations.entry canopy: The canopy over the main entrance. Exact shape is schematic.
explanations.north suite tower: The north wing of duplex suites as one simplified tower block. The hotel holds 202 duplex suites in two wings. Exact floor layout is schematic.
explanations.south suite tower: The south wing of duplex suites as one simplified tower block. Exact floor layout is schematic.
explanations.suite window bands: Bands of suite windows wrapping both tower blocks. Exact window rhythm is schematic.
explanations.backbone spine: The reinforced-concrete spine forming the back of the V behind the suite towers. Exact section is schematic.
explanations.royal penthouse: The Royal Suite, the hotel’s largest at 780 sq m, shown as a penthouse block on the spine. Exact position is schematic.
explanations.tower crown block: The crown blocks capping the suite towers at the top of the accommodation. Exact shape is schematic.
explanations.sail curtain: The double-skinned Teflon-coated woven glass-fibre sail as one billowing curtain, translucent by day and lit as a projection screen at night. Panel count and billow are schematic.
explanations.sail ribs: The horizontal beams the fabric sail is tensioned between, simplified to three ribs. Exact positions are schematic.
explanations.mast needle: The V-shaped steel mast simplified to a single tapered needle rising to the full 321 m height. Exact taper is schematic.
explanations.mast braces: Bracing tying the mast needle against wind loads. Exact pattern is schematic.
explanations.beacon: The aviation warning light on the mast tip. Exact fitting is schematic.
explanations.atrium void: The 180 m tall atrium between the wings as a single void volume. Exact shape is schematic.
explanations.marble pillars: The inclined white-marble-clad columns inside the atrium, simplified to four pillars. Exact positions are schematic.
explanations.sky pod restaurant: Al Muntaha, the restaurant cantilevered 200 m above the sea, merged with the Skyview Bar into one sky pod. Room shape is schematic.
explanations.sky pod arm: The truss cantilevering the sky pod 27 m out from the structure. Exact geometry is schematic.
explanations.tank restaurant: Al Mahara, the seafood restaurant around its aquarium, reached through a simulated submarine voyage. Room shape is schematic.
explanations.fish tank: The Al Mahara aquarium holding about 990,000 litres of seawater behind acrylic glass. Exact tank shape is schematic.
explanations.deck terrace: The North Deck terrace and its pavilion, from the 2016 island extension into the Gulf. Exact outline is schematic.
explanations.helipad disc: The helipad deck at 210 m above ground as a simplified octagonal disc. Exact deck detail is schematic.
explanations.helipad arm: The cantilever truss carrying the helipad out from the structure, simplified to a few struts. Exact geometry is schematic.
explanations.lift shafts: The lift shafts serving the 56 floors, merged into one part. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.plant boxes: The island plant: chillers, generators and water storage merged into one part. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.bridge lights: Lamp columns along the causeway to the shore. Exact positions are schematic.
explanations.pool rectangle: The terrace pool on the deck, standing in for the North Deck pools. Exact shape is schematic.
